1.title: Choosing Data Stores, Caching and Data Lifecycles
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Choosing Data Stores, Caching and Data Lifecycles. It covers the exam area Domain one: Development with A W S Services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Manage data lifecycles with S three Lifecycle policies, T T L and retention periods (one point three.one). Choose A W S data stores based on access patterns (one point three.two). Determine the appropriate caching solution based on data store selection (one point three.three). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain one: Development with A W S Services (thirty percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: Choosing a data store
1.text: Choosing a data store. Files, images, backups, static content. Amazon S three (object storage). Key-value or document lookups at scale, millisecond latency. Amazon Dynamo D B. Relational data, joins, transactions, sequel. Amazon R D S or Amazon Aurora. Very fast reads of hot data, session data. Amazon Elasti Cache (in-memory). Search and log analytics. Amazon Open Search Service. Block storage for one E C two instance. Amazon E B S. Shared file system across instances. Amazon E F S.

1.title: Choosing a data store, continued
1.text: Choosing a data store. The figure shows this: Matching access patterns to data stores. Exam tip: Decide by the access pattern first: lookup by key, sequel joins, large objects, or microsecond caching.

1.title: Caching
1.text: Caching. Amazon Elasti Cache (Redis, Memcached). Caches: Any query result or session. Notes: Redis: data structures, persistence, replication; Memcached: simple, multi-threaded. Dynamo D B Accelerator (D A X). Caches: Dynamo D B reads. Notes: Drop-in for Dynamo D B, no code changes beyond the client; microsecond reads. Amazon Cloud Front. Caches: Web and A P I content at the edge. Notes: Reduces latency and origin load. A P I Gateway cache. Caches: A P I responses per stage. Notes: T T L based.

1.title: Caching strategies
1.text: Caching strategies. Lazy loading (cache-aside). How it works: Read the cache; on a miss, read the database and fill the cache. Trade-off: Only requested data cached; stale data possible. Write-through. How it works: Write the database and the cache together. Trade-off: Cache stays current; writes cost more, cache may hold unused data. T T L. How it works: Each entry expires after a time. Trade-off: Limits staleness. Exam tip: Relational database overloaded by repeated reads equals Elasti Cache. Dynamo D B reads need microseconds with no rewrite equals D A X.

1.title: Data lifecycles
1.text: Data lifecycles. S three Lifecycle policies. Transition objects to cheaper storage classes (for example, Standard to Standard-I A to Glacier) and expire (delete) them after a time. S three versioning. Keep previous versions; lifecycle rules can expire old versions. Dynamo D B T T L. A timestamp attribute marks when an item expires; Dynamo D B deletes it for free in the background. Retention periods. S Q S message retention, Cloud Watch Logs retention, backup retention. Exam tip: A cache cannot fix a bad access pattern: pick the store by how data is read, then add a cache for repeated reads.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An application stores user profile images of varying sizes. Which store fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Amazon S three. S three is object storage for files and images.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A relational database is slow because the same queries repeat constantly. What should the developer add? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Amazon Elasti Cache in front of the database. A cache absorbs repeated reads.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A Dynamo D B-based A P I needs microsecond read latency with minimal code change. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: D A X. D A X is a Dynamo D B-compatible in-memory cache.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Log files must move to cheaper storage after thirty days and be deleted after a year. Which feature handles this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An S three Lifecycle policy. Lifecycle rules transition and expire objects.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Session items in Dynamo D B should disappear automatically after expiry. What should the developer use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: T T L on a timestamp attribute. T T L deletes expired items automatically.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A cache is filled only when data is requested and a miss reads the database. Which strategy is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Lazy loading. That is lazy loading (cache-aside).

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which store suits relational data with joins? Answer: Amazon R D S or Aurora. Question two. What does D A X cache? Answer: Dynamo D B reads. Question three. What is write-through caching? Answer: Writing the database and the cache together.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does an S three Lifecycle policy do? Answer: Transitions objects to other storage classes and expires them. Question five. What does Dynamo D B T T L do? Answer: Deletes items automatically after a timestamp. Question six. Name the two Elasti Cache engines. Answer: Redis and Memcached.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Stores: S three objects, Dynamo D B key-value, R D S or Aurora sequel, Elasti Cache memory. Cache: Elasti Cache (any), D A X (Dynamo D B), Cloud Front (edge), A P I Gateway cache. Strategies: lazy loading, write-through, T T L. Lifecycle: S three Lifecycle, Dynamo D B T T L, retention settings.
